sentences.text: Liaoningosaurus is a basal ankylosaurid dinosaur from Liaoning Province, China, which completely lacks body osteoderms except for a few sub-triangular plates near the neck and shoulder.
The type specimen is estimated to be about 34 centimeters long and is distinctively known for having an osteoderm on its belly.
The premaxilla bears slender teeth with few denticles.
Liaoningosaurus is the oldest known ankylosaurid to possess a tail club.
It is the only known species in its family and genus to possess a ventral osteoderm.
Liaoningosaurus is unusual among ornithischians because preserved stomach contents show it ate fish.
The species was formally described in 2001 by Xing Xu, Xiao-Lin Wang, and Hai-Lu You.
More than 20 specimens of Liaoningosaurus have been found, all representing juvenile individuals identified by unfused neural arches, small size, and lack of post-cervical osteoderms.
A nearly complete skeleton was described in 2016 and later in 2022 from the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning Province.

Specimens have been recovered from the Dawangzhangzi and Jianshangou Beds of the Yixian Formation, and one was retrieved from the Jiufotang Formation of the Jehol Group, living approximately 122 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous.

Researchers suggested Liaoningosaurus was carnivorous, citing fork-like tooth denticles, sharp claws, and fish found within a skeleton, while stomach contents from a second specimen indicate that fish were part of its diet, making it the first known ornithischian adapted to such a lifestyle.
Preserved gut contents suggest Liaoningosaurus may have eaten fish, indicating it hunted or scavenged.

Some scientists conclude that the lack of pelvic fusion and elongated limbs in Liaoningosaurus are adaptations for an aquatic lifestyle, and the proposed semiaquatic adaptation included a 'shell-like' ventral bony plate covering the entire underside of the torso.
Some skeletal features suggest Liaoningosaurus may have been partially aquatic.
Early phylogenetic analyses loosely placed Liaoningosaurus into the family Nodosauridae, and a 2001 cladistic analysis placed it in a primitive branch of the Nodosauridae.
A 2011 cladistic analysis suggested that Liaoningosaurus is a basal member of the Ankylosauridae family.
Liaoningosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous, from approximately 125.4 to 118.9 million years ago.

Researchers debate whether the ventral bony plate is a true bone or merely skin impressions with scales, as broken edges lack bony histology, and a 2014 study reinterpreted the 'shell-like' ventral structure as skin impressions rather than a bony plate, with detailed examination suggesting the ventral 'plates' were likely preserved skin scales rather than bone.

While Ji et al. (2016) argued that Liaoningosaurus specimens were adults, citing unfused ribs and absence of a synsacrum, a 2025 study concluded via bone histology that all known Liaoningosaurus specimens died under one year of age.
